messages:
Alex: quick handoff — I'm primary until 18:00 UTC today. Maya will take primary at 18:00. Jerome is listed as secondary for the whole window.

Alex: Current open alert: intermittent latency spikes for embeddings-service in us-east (INC-245). Pager fired twice in the last 30m but auto-resolved both times. Customer impact currently degraded search relevance for ~3% of requests.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-245 created by alerting rule embeddings-latency-us-east. Severity: P1. Alerts: 2 triggers in 30m. Linked runbook: https://confluence.internal/runbooks/embeddings-latency

Maya: ack — I'm on a short call 17:50-18:20 (may be slow to respond). Can we add a 15m overlap where Jerome is effectively primary 17:45-18:05 to cover my meeting?

Alex: yes, let's do 17:45-18:05 overlap. I'll remain reachable but handing primary to Jerome at 17:45. Jerome?

Jerome: got it. I'll take primary from 17:45-18:05. I'll watch the alert channel and start the warm-handoff checklist now.

Jerome: quick note on diagnostics I ran: increased tail latencies on worker-3 pod (node gpu-a03). KV cache miss rate spiked ~x3. Rolling restart of worker-3 reduced CPU saturation but didn't fully remove p50->p95 gap.

Alex: thanks. Action items: 1) Jerome to continue triage and try isolating request type causing KV misses. 2) If latency >200ms for >15m or customer impact grows >10%, escalate per paging rules below.

Emily: paging rules reminder (copying policy):
- P1 (service degradation impacting >10% requests or any customer-visible outage) — page primary oncall, then page SRE manager (Emma) and AM if customer is paid enterprise.
- If incident persists >15 minutes after first page -> escalate to Eng Lead and infra team, create incident bridge.
- For intermittent spikes with <10% impact, keep in-channel triage, but page SRE lead if recurrence >3 in 1 hour.

Emily: TL;DR: page Emma (SRE manager) for sustained P1 >15m or clear customer outage. Page Eng lead for runbook ops if KV/cache-layer suspected.

Jerome: acknowledging. I'm running these commands now:
```
# check pod cpu/mem and recent restarts
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=embeddings-service -o wide
kubectl -n prod logs embeddings-worker-3 --since=10m
# metric query (internal)
# prometheus: rate(embedding_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]) by (le)
```

Alex: if you hit the threshold to page Emma, also notify the account manager for the affected customer (acct-team@redwood). We should avoid surprises.

Maya: FYI I added a note on my calendar to extend overlap if the incident is still active at 17:40. Also added the runbook link to the handoff doc. :thumbsup:

Jerome: quick repro we saw with a small test payload: embedding length ~6k tokens increases kv-miss dramatically. Suspect cache key hashing regression after the last rollout. I'm going to try a canary rollback on worker-3. If rollback fails, will trigger bridge.

oncall-bot: Runbook step triggered: cache-layer-rollback suggested. Please confirm before running destructive ops.

Jerome: delaying destructive ops until Alex confirms.

Alex: confirmed for canary rollback on worker-3 only. Jerome, start it and post the short command output here. If latency doesn't improve within 5m post-rollback, escalate to Emma and open bridge with "INC-245 embeddings latency - bridge".

Jerome: started canary rollback, command output:
```
rollingupdate.embeddings-worker-3 -> starting rollback
pod embeddings-worker-3-rc3 -> terminated
new pod embeddings-worker-3-rc4 -> running
pod ready after 28s
```

Jerome: p50 looks stable, p95 down ~40% vs last 10m. Keeping watch for 10m to confirm.

Emily: nice work. Once stable, please document root cause hypothesis (cache-key hashing) in the incident doc and schedule a follow-up postmortem if we confirm regression. If it resurfaces, we will have to pin the next release.

Emma: thanks for the heads-up — I'm on-call and reachable. If you escalate, ping me directly and I'll join the bridge. Also confirm whether any enterprise customers need immediate outreach.

Alex: will do. Jerome — keep the channel updated every 5m until handoff to Maya at 18:00, then do a short readout for her. After 18:05 Maya becomes primary and will decide next steps.

Maya: acknowledged. I'll take it from 18:05 and run the follow-up checks. If anything degrades again, I will escalate to Emma.

Alex: final note for handoff checklist (copy to runbook):
- primary, secondary, overlap times noted
- runbook link posted
- rollback performed + evidence posted
- escalate to Emma if >15m or >10% impact
- notify AM for affected customers

Jerome: will add those items in the incident doc now. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-245 status: triage in progress, last update 4m ago. Keep thread for updates.
